title: The Evolutionary Void
author: Hamilton, Peter F.
review:
This was an awesome sci-fi trilogy. Overall I did like this a little less from a character perspective than Pandora's Star / Judas Unchained but there's still a lot of cool sci-fi moments, action, and technology.

Definitely will dig into more Hammy this year, he's a hit with me and is very consistently good overall.

He's also quite unique within the genre and has a good blend of both old and new sci-fi that is very readable and interesting.

highlights.text: Overriding necessity, the siren call of tyrants everywhere.
“Welcome to the paranoia club; cheapest fees in the universe and membership lasts forever.”

Now, I don’t expect you to be gushing with mighty gratitude, but it’s my belief that basic civility will get us all through this without me ripping too many of your fucking limbs off. You clear on this?” “Fascist bastard.”
“What is that Last Dream?” “Nothing,” he whispered. “It showed that even dreams all turn to dust in the end.”
‘The gaiafield was to help people understand and appreciate life, the universe, and everything so they don’t get fooled by idiot messiahs and corrupt politicians.’

Do you understand what that means, you piece of shit? They have been born but two days! Why should I unmake them for you? Eh? Answer me that? Why should I just not exterminate every one of you here and now? That would have the same result. They’ll never be born again, for sure as a genistar shits in the forest,
“I fuck your apology all the way to hell. I hope the warrior Raiel blows your Pilgrimage fleet to shit. The rest of us will have the greatest party history has ever known to celebrate your death.”
But the Void is a beautiful concept; mind over matter is the ultimate evolutionary trait.

“Such a goal is the pinnacle of evolution, elevating an entire universe. We will be the instigators of a genesis from which our mythical gods would cower in awe. Now do you see why I don’t concern myself with the antics of Gore and his kind? I will simply wish them out of existence. And it shall be so.”
“What part of ‘I don’t give up easy’ is hard for you?”
“So if it works, everyone inside the Void will die?” “And the galaxy will live.”

“I did not expect change to befall me ever again,” it told them. “I did not expect to be shown hope, however small. I did not expect to do what I was born to do: to fly against the greatest enemy once more. You have brought this to me. For that I should show thanks. If the galaxy is to fall, then it is fitting that I should fall with it. I will take you.”
“Darkness eclipses us,” it said eventually. “Something is growing outside our frontier, a shroud which would deny us the universe.”
